'''Manfred Steiner''' (November 23, 1931 – January 7, 2023) was an Austrian-born American [[hematologist]] and physicist who taught at [[Brown Medical School]] until 2000.

== Life ==
Steiner was born in [[Vienna]] on November 23, 1931. He earned a medical degree from the [[University of Vienna]] in 1955 and moved to [[Washington, D.C.]] to complete his initial training in internal medicine. Steiner studied [[hematology]] at [[Tufts University]] before earning a Ph.D. in biochemistry from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1967.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brown Physics Student Manfred Steiner Earns Ph.D. at Age 89|url=https://www.brown.edu/news/2021-11-12/steiner|access-date=2024-06-05|website=[[Brown University]]}}</ref>

Steiner moved to [[Rhode Island]] to teach at the [[Alpert Medical School|Medical School]] of [[Brown University]], where he was promoted to full professor in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-11-12|title="If you have a dream, follow it": Man earns Ph.D. in physics at 89|url=https://www.newsweek.com/if-you-have-dream-follow-it-man-earns-phd-physics-89-1648805|access-date=2021-12-12|website=Newsweek|language=en}}</ref> Towards the end of his career, Steiner worked to establish a program in hematology at the University of South Carolina School of Medicine, Greenville. He retired from medicine in 2000.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Chappell|first=Bill|date=2021-11-07|title=He always wanted a Ph.D. in physics. He finally earned it at 89|language=en|work=NPR|url=https://www.npr.org/2021/11/07/1052005447/brown-university-89-phd-physics-dream|access-date=2021-12-13}}</ref>

In September 2021, Steiner completed a Ph.D. in physics at Brown University; his dissertation was entitled ''Corrections to the Geometrical Interpretation of Bosonization.'' Steiner's doctoral advisor was [[Brad Marston]].''<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|title=He always wanted to be a physicist. At 89, he earned his doctorate from Brown.|language=en-US|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/education/2021/11/25/retired-doctor-earns-physics-doctorate-age-89/|access-date=2021-12-12|issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Man fulfills physicist dream, earns Ph.D. at 89|url=https://www.usatoday.com/videos/news/nation/2021/11/11/man-fulfills-physicist-dream-earns-phd-89/6391690001/|access-date=2021-12-13|website=USA TODAY|language=en-US}}</ref>''

He died on January 7, 2023 at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Obituary of Manfred Steiner|publisher=Smith-Mason Funeral Home|url=https://www.smith-masonfuneralhome.com/obituary/Manfred-Steiner|access-date=13 February 2024}}</ref>
